prompt.text: Riya thinks warmer water dissolves a spoon of sugar faster. Which investigation best tests her idea fairly?

options.label: Use equal amounts of water and sugar, change only the water temperature, and compare the dissolving time.
Use different amounts of sugar, different cup sizes and different temperatures at the same time.
Ask several people whether they think warm water should work faster.
Use warm water once and record no measurement.

feedback.correct: Correct. A fair comparison changes the factor being tested while controlling relevant others.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a testable prediction and a fair comparison.

prompt.text: A diet provides plenty of calcium, but a child has very low vitamin D. Why can bone health still be affected?

options.label: Vitamin D helps the body use calcium, so both nutrients matter for healthy bones.
Calcium and vitamin D have no role in bones.
Vitamin D turns calcium into dietary fibre.
Calcium works only when there is no vitamin D.

feedback.correct: Correct. Calcium supports bones and vitamin D helps the body use calcium effectively.
feedback.incorrect: Connect the roles of calcium and vitamin D.

prompt.text: A simple tester needs a part that carries current and an outer handle that reduces current through the hand. Which pairing best fits?

options.label: Use a conductor for the current-carrying part and an insulator for the handle.
Use an insulator for the current path and a conductor for the handle.
Use only materials chosen by colour because electrical properties do not matter.
Use two insulators and expect current to pass easily through both.

feedback.correct: Correct. Conductors allow current relatively easily while insulators resist it.
feedback.incorrect: Match each material role to conductivity or insulation.

prompt.text: Wet clothes dry faster in warm moving air, while droplets form outside a cold glass. Which explanation connects both observations?

options.label: Warmth and moving air can speed evaporation; water vapour can condense to liquid on a cool surface.
Both observations are freezing.
Moving air prevents evaporation and the cold glass creates new water from nothing.
Droplets outside the glass must have leaked through solid glass.

feedback.correct: Correct. The two observations show evaporation and condensation under different conditions.
feedback.incorrect: Identify the change of state in each observation.

prompt.text: A jar contains water with heavy mud particles. Which sequence can make the water clearer using the linked separation ideas?

options.label: Let particles settle, carefully decant the upper liquid, then filter it if finer insoluble particles remain.
Stir continuously so particles cannot settle, then call the mixture separated.
Use only a magnet because all mud is magnetic.
Freeze the jar and assume every impurity disappears.

feedback.correct: Correct. Separation methods can be combined according to particle and mixture properties.
feedback.incorrect: Choose a sequence that uses settling, pouring and filtration appropriately.

prompt.text: Two desert animals are grouped together because they share several body features, but one has a special water-saving feature. What is the best interpretation?

options.label: Classification uses shared characteristics, while an adaptation can help an organism survive in its environment.
Being in the same group means every adaptation must be identical.
Adaptations cannot be used to understand organisms.
Classification groups organisms randomly without comparing features.

feedback.correct: Correct. Classification and adaptation answer related but different biological questions.
feedback.incorrect: Separate the idea of shared characteristics from survival adaptations.

prompt.text: A bar magnet breaks into two pieces. What should you expect when testing the pieces?

options.label: Each piece still has two poles, so like poles can repel and unlike poles can attract.
One piece becomes only north and the other only south.
Both pieces permanently lose every magnetic pole.
All poles attract one another regardless of type.
